statement: f05's route-plan lives entirely under crates/enforcer-scan/src/router/{detect,scope,plan,native_tie}.rs, sibling files added to the arc-15 router/mod.rs skeleton (which already defines the coarse LanguageFamily/classify pair f05 does not touch). detect.rs defines its own richer DetectedLanguage enum (Rust/TypeScript/Python/Dart/Go/Cfml/Other) fed by manifest-basename sniffing (Cargo.toml, package.json, tsconfig.json, pyproject.toml, setup.py, pubspec.yaml, go.mod, box.json) plus enforcer_literal_scan's extension map; scope.rs defines RouteScope (Repo|Workspace|Crate|Package|Folder|Domain|Diff, default Repo) as a narrowing-only filter distinct from crate::scope's tri-modal CLI resolver; plan.rs's build_route_plan(paths, &RouteScope, &ResolvedProjectTie) -> RoutePlan is the single serializable entry point every consumer should call.
why: f01 already owns modes.rs in the same crate and the workpack mandated file-disjointness; router/mod.rs's doc comment explicitly reserves deeper per-family adapters for f05 as sibling files, so extending rather than replacing the skeleton kept both lanes non-conflicting and matched the documented seam.
howToApply: Consumers (f01 modes, check/scan/run MCP tools, c04 deny-hook) should call enforcer_scan::router::plan::build_route_plan(&walked_paths, &route_scope, &resolved_tie) to get languages/rule_packs/native_tools, never hardcode a language or reimplement detection.

statement: enforcer_config::project_tie::ResolvedNativeTie does not derive Serialize/Deserialize (it is an internal resolver output, not a wire type), so a serializable RoutePlan cannot embed it directly. f05 solved this by defining its own small serializable mirror, router::native_tie::RouteTie{mode: NativeMode, scope: EnforcerScope} (both of which DO derive Serialize/Deserialize in project_tie.rs), and copying the two fields across at construction time rather than editing enforcer-config (out of f05's owns set) to add derives.
why: Adding Serialize/Deserialize to ResolvedNativeTie would touch a file f05 does not own (crates/enforcer-config/src/project_tie.rs), violating the workpack's exact-file-claims discipline; a local flat projection is a one-file, zero-cross-lane-conflict fix.
howToApply: When a route-plan or similar cross-crate serializable struct needs to carry a resolver's decision from a crate you do not own, define a small local mirror struct with only the fields you need (deriving Serialize/Deserialize locally) rather than editing the upstream crate's internal type.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-scan/src/router/native_tie.rs RouteTie + cargo build -p enforcer-scan error E0277 (Serialize not satisfied for ResolvedNativeTie) before the fix

statement: Literal-scan (arc-13, enforcer-literal-scan) treats every file as scannable via detect_language(path, include_unknown=true) even when the extension is not in its own ~65-entry language_registry() — it falls back to a Fallback-family LanguageSpec rather than skipping the file. f05's router mirrors this: any extensioned file that isn't a manifest basename and doesn't map to a T1-packed DetectedLanguage variant (Rust/TypeScript/Python/Dart/Go/Cfml) contributes DetectedLanguage::Other, which routes to RulePack::LiteralScanFloor only, never a T1 blocker. A manifest file's own extension (e.g. Cargo.toml's .toml) is explicitly excluded from also contributing Other, so a rust-only repo with just a Cargo.toml doesn't spuriously detect a second 'language'.
why: Getting this wrong (treating unrecognized-by-registry extensions as 'nothing detected') would silently under-scan files literal-scan itself would have scanned, breaking the acceptance criterion that an unknown ext must still carry the literal-scan T2 floor, never a false empty route.
howToApply: When routing or classifying files by extension against the literal-scan registry, always treat 'not in the registry' as 'still gets the universal floor', not as 'skip this file' — only a manifest-basename match (already counted) or a truly extensionless, non-manifest basename should contribute zero detection.
